dosejournal_reflectiontext_edcdaf: Describe your experience during the dosing session from beginning to end with as much detail as possible:  I went through 5 unique "waves" of memories, thoughts and impact waves from the drug.  The waves felt like a wave of thought and memories flowing over me while my mask was on, and I was able to sort and think through the thoughts with an organized process. In between the waves I was able to take the mask off, process and talk briefly with the facilitators and then would put the mask back on as I was ramping back up.  1. The first wave was organizing my thoughts into a dock or multiple tabs type screen on a computer. I would close my eyes and be able to see thoughts come up on the screen and then decide whether to view them or move them to the side, minimize them or bring them into my focus and think about them. It felt good to be able to control my thoughts and decide which ones to pursue or which ones to ignore or move aside in the moment.  2. The second wave was focused on exploring memories from my family, childhood & family tree. I realized that the family tree was supporting me and my immediate family and we had in some ways turned away and focused inward on ourselves instead of putting energy back towards the tree.  3. The third was was reflecting on my back pain. I was able to follow the pain from my back through my nerves into my head where I was feeling the pain. I was also able to view how my pain was influencing my parents, my wife, and my kids.   4. The fourth wave was a realization that I am not building community that I want to be building. I saw an image of friends around a campfire and realized I am not creating spaces for those opportunities in this season at all and want to.  5. The 5th wave was really just empty headspace/meditation. I didn't have any thoughts entering my mind and was able to just be without interruption. It felt restful and energizing, like a 4 hour nap in 15 minutes.    Describe your emotions, energy levels, and thoughts during and after the dosing session:     During the session I was tired but overall had energy to engage. Afterwards I was talkative, energetic and then got tired and weary as the evening went on.    Describe if you encountered any challenging emotions, insights, or sensations throughout the session:   Several of the topics discussed lead me to realize that there are several aspects of my life that I am not living out the way I would want to - and this was challenging and vulnerable to realize.    Summarize any changes in health that may occur since the dosing session:  I have had a headache the past few days since dosing and have felt tight in my back and neck. Not abnormal to some weeks before dosing.  Immediately after dosing I felt dizzy and lightheaded for the remainder of the day and felt a little chemically unbalanced - almost hungover.

ir_report: Zach Busby was the first to became aware on January 15th, 2024 following an email from Dr. Boris Heifets regarding a new participant's eligibility.
ir_summary: On January 15th 2024, Dr. Boris Heifets sent an email regarding a new participant's eligibility. Upon review of Stanford's screening measures for that participant, Zach Busby noticed that the procedures had been completed outside the protocol's allowance of a "maximum of 60 days pre V7," the day of psilocybin dosing.    This event prompted review of the timing of screening procedures for the other participants, all of whom had already been dosed. Sophie Bax discovered that several of the screening procedures for POP1008 were also completed outside of the 60 day window. More specifically, the medical exam and medical history were completed on August 10th, 2023, 98 days before dosing, and the psychological assessments were completed on August 14th, 2023, 94 days before dosing.    Though this constitutes a deviation from the protocol's 60 day allowance, the procedures required to ensure the safety of proceeding with a psilocybin dose, the MADRS and HAM-A psychological assessments, are repeated at the V3 Baseline visit, which occurs 1-2 weeks before dosing. For POP1008, these assessments took place on November 2nd, only 14 days prior to his dosing session.     The other screening procedures that were completed outside of the 60 day window and not subsequently repeated, including the SCID and medical exam, are considered clinically valid for 12 months, though the study team prefers to collect them within 6 months of the dosing date. Therefore, these initial screening procedures were also sufficient for accurately determining the safety of proceeding with a psilocybin dose.     Because this deviation did not result in meaningful substantive harm to the participant or affect the integrity of the data collected, the study team determined it to be a minor protocol violation that does not require clinical follow-up and is not reportable. The study team is working on clarifying the language in the protocol and will submit an IRB modification accordingly.

ir_report: Zach Busby was the first to became aware on January 15th, 2024 following an email from Dr. Boris Heifets regarding this participant's eligibility.
ir_summary: On January 15th 2024, Dr. Boris Heifets sent an email to the UCSF study team regarding the eligibility of POP1010. Upon review of Stanford's screening measures, Zach Busby noticed that the procedures had been completed more than 60 days prior to the planned dosing date for this participant, which is not in accordance with the protocol's allowance of a "maximum of 60 days pre V7," the dosing date.      The Stanford study team repeated all the screening measures on January 11th, 2024 and January 24th, 2024, well within the 60 day mark of the planned dosing date of February 29th, with the exception of the SCID. However, the SCID is considered clinically valid for up to 12 months. It could therefore be used to accurately determine the safety of proceeding with a psilocybin dose for this participant in combination with the repeated screening measures.     Because this deviation did not result in meaningful substantive harm to the participant or affect the integrity of the data collected, the study team determined it to be a minor protocol violation that does not require clinical follow-up and is not reportable. The study team is working on clarifying the language in the protocol and will submit an IRB modification accordingly.

ae_description: Participant reported mild fatigue due to long working hours. Fatigue lasted one day and resolved on its own.
Participant reported mild constipation that she described as "within the range of normal." Resolved without medication or treatment.

6 hours after the time of drug administration, the participant reported a headache that she rated a 7/10. Participant has reported a history of chronic migraines and stated that she arrived at the research unit with a headache prior to dosing that she rated as a 4/10. After eating a light snack while still at the research unit, the participant reported that the headache decreased back to 4/10, which she described as her "normal" or "baseline."    During her integration 1 session on 3/1/24, participant reported that the headache spiked again the evening after dosing, reaching an 8/10, but returned to her baseline 4/10 headache the morning of 3/1/24. Participant declined taking any pain medication other than her prescribed regimen of tizanidine and gabapentin.
ae_intervention_notes: Continuing her prescribed regimen of tizanidine and gabapentin, as well as herbal remedies including lemon.

ae_description: Participant reported a feeling like her feet were "thawing" after arriving home following her dosing session. She described the feeling as "tingling" that lasted for about an hour and resolved on its own. She endorsed a history of "mild Reynauds" to Aliss during her integration session.     The participant reported being very cold during her dosing session, but stated she did not notice the feet tingling until she arrived at home.

Participant described feeling like she "had no energy" and was "tapped" after the dosing session. She reported awaking this morning "not feeling like [she] slept well." She also described feeling "almost like [she] was hungover" and "like [her] body had been beaten up."     She rated it as "mild" in the elicited event tracking questionnaire.    Per conversation on 3/4/2024, participant reported feeling "quite well" on Saturday 3/2/24.

Participant reported waking on 3/1/24, the morning after dosing, with widespread body pain. She rated the pain upon waking at a 5/10 but stated that it had decreased to a 3/10 over the course of the morning. She stated that her back pain was not worse than normal.    She reported first noticing pain in her left shoulder towards the end of the dosing session, as well as a heightened sense of awareness of her back pain while under the effects of psilocybin.    During a conversation on 3/4/2024, the participant reported that pain had subsided midday on 3/2/2024

dosejournal_reflectiontext_edcdaf: -10 minutes after dosing I did experience mild tingling throughout my body. This was a new feeling I have not experienced previously in my life.    -I was then asked to lay down and put on the mask and listen to music. I just started to meditate. I did see mild, moving grayscale shadows but that is typical when I go into deep meditation. I never felt any cognitive psychedelic affects at all. I continued to meditate throughout the day with no other changes.    -I tried to keep my emotions neutral so that any medicine I took would guide me. I did not really feel that that occurred however. My energy level was normal for me with no significant observable change on my part. My thoughts throughout the day were to continue meditating while waiting for a psychedelic experience. That never occurred.    -After 2 to 3 hours or so it became evident to me that I did not appear to be responding to a "psychedelic meaningful experience"    -I had no new sensations for remainder of the day and just continue to meditate.    -I am not aware of any changes in my health since the dosing session.

ir_report: Amber McKernan was the first person to become aware of this event.  Amber became aware of this event on November 1st, 2023.  This event began on November 1st, 2023.
ir_summary: - Amber McKernan became aware of this during the V8 visit when collecting the medication record.  - The participant reported a new medication that he did not mention during all other medication check reviews. He reported taking one 50mg tablet of trazodone on 10/31/2023 to help him with sleep. He mentioned being prescribed 50mg trazodone for sleep as needed over a year ago and only have taken it "a few times."  - Trazodone is an exclusionary medication. The participant is not supposed to take trazodone during study participant. If the participant had reported the medication at his screening, like he was supposed to, the study doctor would have informed him he is unable to take this medication during study participation. The participant would have to agree to not take this medication during the study in order to be eligible for study participation.  - It has resolved. Study doctors followed up with the participant asking him to withhold the medication for the rest of the duration of the study. However, the participant had hesitancy around withholding Trazodone. The study team agreed to not discontinue the participation , and agreed it was safe for him to continue. We asked the participant to report to us if he does take another does of trazodone, he agreed.

ir_report: Zach Busby was the first to became aware on January 15th, 2024 following an email from Dr. Boris Heifets regarding a new participant's eligibility.
ir_summary: On January 15th 2024, Dr. Boris Heifets sent an email regarding a new participant's eligibility. Upon review of Stanford's screening measures for that participant, Zach Busby noticed that the procedures had been completed outside the protocol's allowance of a "maximum of 60 days pre V7," the day of psilocybin dosing.    This event prompted review of the timing of screening procedures for the other participants, all of whom had already been dosed. Sophie Bax discovered that several of the screening procedures for POP1011, including the SCID, psychological assessments, and medical exam/history, were completed on August 16, 2023, 71 days before his dose on October 26, 2023.     Though this constitutes a deviation from the protocol's 60 day allowance, the procedures required to ensure the safety of proceeding with a psilocybin dose, the MADRS and HAM-A psychological assessments, are repeated at the V3 Baseline visit, which occurs 1-2 weeks before dosing. For POP1011, these assessments took place on October 18th, 2023, only 6 days prior to his dosing session.     The other screening procedures that were completed outside of the 60 day window and not subsequently repeated are considered clinically valid for 12 months, though the study team prefers to collect them within 6 months of the dosing date. Therefore, in addition to the repeated psychological assessments, these initial screening procedures were also sufficient for accurately determining the safety of proceeding with a psilocybin dose.     Because this deviation did not result in meaningful substantive harm to the participant or affect the integrity of the data collected, the study team determined it to be a minor protocol violation that does not require clinical follow-up and is not reportable. The study team is working on clarifying the language in the protocol and will submit an IRB modification accordingly.

dosejournal_reflectiontext_edcdaf: It was very pleasant. I don't remember much except that I was surprised how wobbly I was when I needed to get up and walk to the bathroom. I appreciated the assistance (arm for support).  I was happy that Aliss took notes on everything I said as I often felt that what I wanted her to record was important, even though I didn't remember most of what I said. I did remember appreciating my mother's courage as a civil rights activist and being angry that the minister at her funeral did not capture the courage and feistiness of my mother's character.   I laid down for most of the session and felt very relaxed/low energy. I felt happy, mellow, and content. I had thoughts of being grateful for my life.    I forgot to bring my carefully prepared snacks/fruit and had not eaten before I arrived. I remember being very hungry and disappointed in the stale nuts and oreo cookies that were brought to me.   I was disturbed by the country music/banjo piece of music that was played near the end of the session (I believe). I asked Aliss if she could skip that track and she said she could not. I worked through my aversion to the piece of music which arose from my history of being taught by my parents that all  country music is played by dangerous racists. Although I've worked through that generalization and have come to appreciate some country music, I still have an initial reaction to country music that triggers fear and feelings of danger, especially since my husband is black. If we walk into a bar or restaurant playing country music we usually leave immediately just to be safe. I asked him what it would be like if he was in an altered state from psilocybin and heard a piece of country music. He said it would be extremely unpleasant. I would suggest that the program reconsider that particular piece of music and consider removing it, especially if you hope to have any POC/African American participants.    I believe that my back had less pain at the end of the session, but I can't remember for sure.

ir_report: Zach Busby was the first to became aware on January 15th, 2024 following an email from Dr. Boris Heifets regarding a new participant's eligibility.
ir_summary: On January 15th 2024, Dr. Boris Heifets sent an email regarding a new participant's eligibility. Upon review of Stanford's screening measures for that participant, Zach Busby noticed that the procedures had been completed outside the protocol's allowance of a "maximum of 60 days pre V7," the day of psilocybin dosing.    This event prompted review of the timing of screening procedures for the other participants, all of whom had already been dosed. Sophie Bax discovered that several of the screening procedures for POP1020 were also completed outside of the 60 day window. More specifically, the medical exam and medical history were completed on September 29th, 2023, 69 days before dosing, and the psychological assessments were completed on October 4th, 2023, 64 days before dosing.    Though this constitutes a deviation from the protocol's 60 day allowance, the procedures required to ensure the safety of proceeding with a psilocybin dose, the MADRS and HAM-A psychological assessments, are repeated at the V3 Baseline visit, which occurs 1-2 weeks before dosing. For POP1020, these assessments took place on November 29th, only 8 days prior to her dosing session.     The other screening procedures that were completed outside of the 60 day window and not subsequently repeated, including the SCID and medical exam, are considered clinically valid for 12 months, though the study team prefers to collect them within 6 months of the dosing date. Therefore, these initial screening procedures were also sufficient for accurately determining the safety of proceeding with a psilocybin dose.     Because this deviation did not result in meaningful substantive harm to the participant or affect the integrity of the data collected, the study team determined it to be a minor protocol violation that does not require clinical follow-up and is not reportable. The study team is working on clarifying the language in the protocol and will submit an IRB modification accordingly.

ae_description: Participant reported when they arrived at 8:00 that they came in with a "pit in their stomach."    At 10:00, participant went to the restroom and returned feeling nauseous. Participant purged intermittently at this time. Emesis bag was utilized; participant was told to take slow breaths.    Participant vomited intermittently from 10:00-11:00. BP was tracked and participant was told to take slow breaths again.     Vomiting resolved around 11:00.    Nausea resolved around 16:00.
ae_intervention_notes: Deep breathing, relaxation techniques with facilitators

ae_description: At 16:00 on dosing day, participant reported an emerging 3/10 intensity headache along with agitation and anxiety.     Participant took excedrin when they got home at 18:45. At this time and the headache along with agitation was reportedly resolving.    Participant said at their Integration visit her headaches are back to normal intensity and does not feel that she needs to take another Excedrin at this time.

Participant reported at their integration 1 session that when she woke up, she has felt moderate dissociation to the point where she is unable to concentrate on her normal everyday tasks. She said she feels like she is "out of her own body."    She expressed worry about picking up her car from the service center later, as she is unsure she will be able to focus and interact with the employees. Participant also said if she had to work today she would "be unable to do any of her tasks" because she consistently feels spaced out and disconnected from her own body.     Participant plans on taking it easy the rest of the day and laying down.    Participant reported at her V9 phone call that she is still experiencing mild dissociation and concentration problems. When she is at work and she needs to report a paragraph back in Spanish she finds difficulty remembering what was originally said. She says she is "not 100% back on her game" at work, but has not needed to take time off    Participant reported at her V10 visit that she is still having trouble concentrating and remembering details at work that she would normally not struggle with. She said her co-workers have not noticed a difference in her ability but she feels personally that she is struggling.     Participant reported at her integration 3 session that she is "back at a zero" and she no longer suffers from any concentration. She mentioned she probably had it resolve around 05/09.

Participant reported during her integration 1 session feeling a tremor in her hands that started at the end of the dosing session and has continued until now.    When the participant tries to reach for something, her hands begin shaking, and she is unable to keep her hands still. Participant feels "weakness and frailness" and wonders if the tremors are from anxiety post-dosing. Participant said that the tremors have been the same since the end of dosing and have not gotten better or worse.    Participant reported that the tremors have stopped and she has not experienced any recently.

After dosing around 9:30pm when the participant returned home, she reported feeling a heart palpitation for about 1 minute. Participant says she has not felt a palpitation for many years before this.     The palpitation resolved after the participant sat down and has not happened again since the first instance.

Participant reported feeling digestive problems after dosing on the car ride home. She describes it as "the need to relieve myself but I am unable to." When the participant arrived home, she experienced diarrhea that she described as "not typical diarrhea."    Participant took a probiotic supplement to help her bowel movement.    When she woke up this morning, she reported immediately feeling like she had diarrhea again and that her stool is loose. She is unsure if probiotic is helping and has not been able to use the bathroom yet today and says these digestive problems are disrupting her ability to focus on her daily tasks.    At her V9 phone call, participant reported that her stool is still a different color and she feels like her bowel movements have not returned to normal yet.    Participant reported at her V10 visit that her digestive issues are resolving and slowly she has returned to normal. She no longer has the feeling of needing to use the restroom constantly.

dosejournal_reflectiontext_edcdaf: I'm going to start with when I feel like I first felt the medications have an effect. That feels like it was about 20 minutes after I first swallowed the capsules, and I felt a bit of a jolt, similar to the feeling that I get when my Imitrex starts to take effect. Then, maybe about 5 to 10 minutes later, I started to feel a slight warmth or flush on my face, but it took a while to feel any psychedelic effects. At first, I thought that I had probably gotten as low of a dose as possible because it seemed like a while before I felt anything.    The transition from feeling nothing to experiencing psychedelic effects was very abrupt. It went from 0 to 100 very suddenly, and what I started seeing was very rapidly moving, very intricate colored patterns. It was not like a kaleidoscope, but it was more like observing a ceiling of a mosque starting to move and weave in and out of itself. I remember the patterns had lots of blues, reds, and creams; it seemed like a mix of patterns that you might see on a tile with a jeweled border, and they were moving around each other. The borders were kind of moving and flowing around, and it was happening very rapidly in pace with the music.    The patterns were very abstract and changed color and motif with the music, so if I was listening to music that seemed sort of indigenous, then the patterns would also seem more indigenous, and things that were more, say, Central Asian had more of a Central Asian motif. There was also a period where I wished I could have gotten up and danced with the music, when it had an upbeat tempo. I also recall the visuals become less colorful and grey when the music was somber.    About maybe 20 or 30 minutes after the patterns started, I started to feel pretty nauseous and had to turn over and lay on my left side to deal with the nausea.     I could hear what was going on in the room the whole time; I could hear pages turning, I could hear people going in and out of the bathroom, or opening other doors. I could also hear the construction that was happening, but because I was most comfortable laying on my side, I did not want to put the big headphones on.    I do remember one recurring motif was that there were bright, rainbow-colored, very narrow threads that I interpreted to be a visualization of nerve signals or nerve sensations. I found those threads to come back periodically throughout the entire session. I also found them to be protective, and that they seemed to be a border. There was one time when I felt like the motif I was visualizing had me descending into a darker part of the field, and that the rainbow nerve bands kept snapping me back upwards.    I feel like, at all times, I was aware I was in the room and that I was lying on the sofa, but at times, my mind's view felt much bigger. At all times, I felt like I was an observer of what I was seeing in my mind, and I was not participating in the patterns, and they were not a physical experience.    I recall when I had to get up and go to the bathroom, sort of in the middle of it, I felt very light-headed, and I did not see the patterns when I had my eyes open, and I was like in the bathroom, but there were, there was a feeling of waviness, of like, for example, the lines in the tile kind of moving back and forth.    I only recall having one memory surface that was based on an actual life event, and that was a memory about taking a trip to the Santa Cruz Natural Arch State Park with my kids when they were younger, and my son falling while he was climbing and hitting his head. It wasn't traumatic in any way, and it was a very vivid memory, but it just came and went. I didn't quite understand why I was recalling that memory, other than feeling confused about how he had injured himself; at the time, in real-life, there was no confusion.    At times, I tried to direct the sensations of observation to areas where I am experiencing pain, primarily in my face and in my back, and I wasn't able to gain any understanding or direct what I was observing towards the pain, or towards creating a visualization of the pain, or being able to manage the pain in any way.     I remember feeling a little frustrated that I couldn't visualize where the pain was happening and try to mentally reduce the level of pain I was feeling in certain areas, and then just like giving up and trying to give in to just observing and experiencing the hallucinogens.     At no time did I feel particularly scared or fearful, or excited, or really any sort of extreme of emotions. It was more like I was just there, experiencing this happening to me.    Towards the end of the session, I started to feel my first physical sensations linked with this hallucinations (other than the nausea earlier), and that was a feeling of the small muscles around my ears flexing, like when you try to pop your ears, and that kept happening over and over again. It started to get irritating and somewhat painful. And it was something that would go across my face over and over, and I would hear the kind of crunchy crackling of those tendons around the ears, but also across my cheeks, and I started to want to massage the muscles around my right ear because they were feeling sore and painful.    As the patterns started to decrease, I could tell that I was starting to come out of the hallucinogenic portion of the session. I felt very thirsty, I felt a little headachey, and a little tired. I remember after I sat up and started to have a snack, I started to feel very happy, more happy than I have felt in a long time. I was surprised by that. The feeling of happiness stayed with me for about an hour or so.    The drive home after the session was uneventful. Eva and I just talked about work, and life, and family things. It took about 2 hours to get home, which is not bad, all things considered. When I got home, I was starting to feel more pain in the right side of my jaw, and in an area where I don't typically experience pain, so it was more like back towards the actual hinge of my jaw, rather than in my face. I had dinner and then just relaxed and went to bed early.    When I woke up the next morning, I had a bad migraine and ended up having to take two 50 mg doses of Imitrex because it did not go away after the first one. That is not very typical for me these days, so it was a pretty bad headache. My jaw remained sore throughout the day, so much so that I tried using heat packs and ice packs, and I took some Tylenol. I felt completely back to normal, and I have not noticed any change or impact on the areas of my body where I typically have pain, except for the new occurrence of pain in my right jaw.    If I had to guess I would say that I did not receive a high dose of psilocybin. I did not hear any sounds that weren't already in the room, I did not experience any visions, nor any access to deep feelings or experiences. It was all so abstract. I'm also surprised that in the end I ended up with more pain than I started because of the problems with my jaw. This is not an experience that I would seek to repeat.

ae_title: Tingling in right ring and pinky finger
ae_description: Participant reported constant tingling in her right hand, localized to her ring and pinky finger. She described it as not interfering with her daily life but stated that it does provoke anxiety as she does not know what is causing it. She reported that the tingling began 3 years ago.     Participant reported seeing a neurologist who performed an inconclusive nerve conduction test. She stated that her neurologist believes it to be related to a nerve in her elbow or spine.     3 month:   Stayed the same
ae_intervention_notes: No interventions/therapies have been administered for this complaint.

ae_description: At her baseline visit, the participant reported difficulty sleeping that she rated as "moderate." At her prep 2 visit on 3/27, the participant reported worsening sleep issues due to the discontinuation of the THC/CBD gummy that she takes for sleep on 3/24 (as required for study participation). She stated that the sleep issues were still "within the range of normal."     Participant reported on 4/1 that the sleep issues resolved the night after dosing when she took the THC/CBD gummy again.
Participant described feeling mildly nauseated during dosing session. Participant turned her physical body's position to the side.    Nausea resolved after participant changed positions.

Participant reported significant tension and pain on the right side of her jaw, concentrated near the right ear. Participant stated that she began to feel the pain near bedtime the evening after dosing. She described the sensation as a "constant aching" and stated it was tender to the touch. She rated the pain as an 8/10 at its worst and a 7/10 at the time of asking. She reported that the pain radiated to the midline of her face at its worst. She has a history of TMJ per medical history documentation.    She reported taking extra strength Tylenol (2x 500mg) as needed for the pain as well as alternating heat and ice packs.     As of 4/15, the participant reported that the surface area and the intensity of the pain have gone down. She rated the pain a 5/10, stating that it was still worse than pre-dosing face pain of 4/10. She reported discontinuing Tylenol as it was not effective.     On 4/25, the participant reported experiencing a muscle spasm on the same side of her face as the jaw pain, but stated that the overall pain level has not changed.     3 month:  Jaw pain has gone from 4-5 on average before dosing to an 8-9 after dosing and is now down to a 6 for most of May and June, but still not as it was before dosing. Pt tried two new medications: Oxcarbazepine which she stopped after a week, and and gabapentin which she started at the beginning of June. She has not noticed a difference yet.
ae_intervention_notes: Medical visit completed with participant, summary: Pain is self-limited and slowly resolving. Described as musculoskeletal pain. No concerning features for other neurologic or cardiovascular pathology. Participant planning to undergo acupuncture which has previously helped myofascial pain flares. Participant was provided direct contact information for study physicians, who will follow up in two weeks if they have not made contact prior to that date.

ae_description: Participant reported waking up with a migraine on 3/29, the day after her dosing session. Participant has endorsed history of chronic migraines, but described this migraine as worse than her standard migraine. She rated the migraine as moderate. The participant reported taking 50 mg of Imitrex on Friday morning but stated that it was not sufficient so she took another 50 mg, after which the migraine subsided. She stated it is unusual for her to need the full 100 mg.     She reported that the migraine returned on the morning of Saturday, 3/30, and she took another 50 mg of Imitrex, after which the migraine resolved and has not returned.

Participant reported that the frequency of her migraines has increased from 1-2 per month to 1 per week since her dose on 3/28. She stated that the intensity is the same as it was before dosing. She reported continuing her standard treatment regimen of 50 mg of Imitrex.       3 month follow up:  Pt reported same number of migraines. Pt said they have "gotten worse in terms of severity but not frequency."  In May, Pt experienced a visual aura during a migraine which has only happened once before.

dosejournal_reflectiontext_edcdaf: Leaned into feelings of authenticity and experience of self.  Comfortably existing in my own realm.     Playing with sound and color that became energy and frequency. I was able to manipulate it with my hands.     Circuitry and wiring (information?). Following the winding bending pathways of tubing/information (?)... in a physical flowing feeling like a quick gentle rollercoaster.     The feeling as if I was existing between spaces. For a little while it felt and looked like I was inside of a speaker or under a sound stage or inside the workings of a bigger machine.  The colors were deep purples and blues. It was quite intense, but I found it very interesting.     The most difficult part was the transition between sitting/laying down to standing. I was really annoying by the contrast of how fluid my mind was compared to how stiff, achy and crunchy my body was. It was very jarring.     Near the beginning I found the answer to what is at the end of the tunnel I see when I meditate. The answer is "it's not what at the end, it is what is inside" and I was shown the sides of the tunnel rippling with layers of patterns and colors... that also had their own tunnels (portals?). There were a lot of out loud "WOW's!!" at this point. Truly stunning visuals. I became overwhelmed (in a good way) with all the best emotions and a feeling of physical lightness.     After a trip 'into the unknown' aka the bathroom... I was able to enjoy looking at the piece of resin art I recently made and brought with me. I watched it unfold back to the beginning of its creation. I now have a better understanding of the process of resin pouring and how it's moves and flows before it cures. Since this medium is fairly new to me I found this experience to be extremely helpful and have made 8 pieces since Thursday (it's now Sunday).  I also figured out how to incorporate the wire work pieces I make into the resin pieces-a problem that has been stuck in its process for a while.     Looking at this piece gave me a lot of joy and elation. I wanted to exist in art forever.  I began to see everything as art. I had a flash of a talk Ram Dass gives were his friend repeats "Extraordinary!!" .. I felt like that guy.  I wished I could listen to some Ram Dass talks at that moment, but he did show up in the playlist later... which kind of blew my mind because of all of the feelings of connectedness I was experiencing.  I kept seeing how things from a few days .. even weeks ago we're all involved and seemed purposefully laid out and placed into this and future moments in time. I recall saying time feels more like a spiral and not a straight line- it makes more sense that way.      After getting acclimated from another trip to the bathroom (where everything looked visually cubed. I thought the folks who designed the game Minecraft were genius for marketing a psychedelic experience.)    I got laid down and got comfortable and began to jump into what felt like different bubbles. Each bubble had its own vibe and color way. I didn't meet any other people or entities there. It was just me exploring these spaces. I really enjoyed the pink and gold bubble. It felt like a memory.. like I had existed there sometime long ago before this visit.     Being able to see through the eye mask was absolutely incredible.  It really bent my mind... are eyeballs just an illusion to placate our human bodies? Why do I have to wear these glasses if I can see through an eye mask?     I also had a while where I was seeing two separate color and pattern situations with each eye. Very chameleon like.  Somehow it felt like I was existing in between these to spaces... another mind bending experience.     At some point as I was drifting through colors, patterns and textures I found myself looking down at my feet. They were standing on small white crystals that I soon recognized as salt. When I looked up I saw a very large lake drying up right before my eyes and leaving the remains of salt crystal. I knew I'd been there before or somewhere similar, but I couldn't remember when or what it was called. I asked Aliss and Taylor to make a note of this so I could think about it after this experience.     I've never been to the Sultan Sea.. in person, but I really do feel like I have been or have some sort of connection there... so odd.     Layers of colors, textures and patterns continued throughout the experience along with continuous physical feelings of flowing movement, vibrating energy and a sense that the top of my head had warm glitter beaming straight out of it.     I experienced deep emotions of Awe, Love, Wonder, Curiosity, Oneness, Connections, Connectivity.. and a sense and knowing that everything happens and is happening for a reason.✨    Since Thursday, I have felt very relaxed despite the mild head ache I had Friday. I am feeling a little more tired than usual. Meditating has been delightfully peaceful the past few mornings. My mind quiets quickly and stays still for longer periods of time. The Oura ring is still picking up my meditation time as REM and light sleep.     I am not feeling any more or less body/back pain than usual at this time.

dosejournal_reflectiontext_edcdaf: 8am: Arrived to the Nancy UCSF Psych building.  My room was set up for me, Gisele and Rosanna met me in the lobby.  We went to the basement, they had their own crystals already set out, so I got mine out (as well as my other chosen tokens, a mushroom fairy door, and my "trans joy" bracelet).  I also got out my blankets and a change of clothes, in case I wanted it.  I did a meditation, guided by Gisele.  It was soft and gentle, welcoming my body to the space and present moment.  We talked about my outstanding anxieties, especially around the unknown dosages and combination of drugs I was about to receive, and centered myself to the experience.  I did a urine test to clear me to dose.  Then, Gisele brought in the medicine.      9am: She gave me the 6 pills out of a shell, which I took, and then immediately dropped the shell, instant embarrassment.  I hate feeling clumsy.  She reassured me it was NO problem, that all was well.  Down the hatch, as they say.  I reassured myself that I was safe, despite not knowing exactly what I just took, and settled into the couch, knowing I could start to feel the effects in as little as 15 minutes, or as long as an hour.  I didn't know what to do until they kicked in, so Gisele offered some choices, one of which was her reading some poems to me, Mary Oliver and Rumi.  She read 3, one of which was about welcoming spiritual visitors, no matter how scary.  This felt especially poignant, and set the tone for the day.  I felt a sense of relaxation, so I put the eyeshades on, and the headphones, and closed my eyes, waiting for lift-off.  I tried to meditate on my breath.      Soon enough, it was time to take my blood pressure for the first time.  I noticed I was not feeling the psilocybin at this point, and rated my experience a 0/10 at that point.  I continued to relax, listening to the music, mulling over my intentions (to let go and give into the experience), and thinking "I must have been microdosed".  I also thought, "now that I've thought of that, it's probably a famous last words situation..." (I was right, about the latter).  Time began to pass slowly.  There was a song with rushing water, or maybe a few, and suddenly, I had the urge to go pee.  I think I was a bit restless, waiting for it to start.  I rushed my stand and walked, and had to take a break in the hallway, seeing stars, feeling like I might pass out.  After the stars subsided, I went to the bathroom, and noticed when I was washing my hands that my eyes had not yet begun to dilate.  Still early.  The walls in the bathroom were not yet breathing.    Sometime later, it was time for the second BP, at this point, I was up to a 2/10, I was noticing a pull to my inner world and a little softness to my surroundings.  I asked what time it was, Gisele told me it was "still very early" (or maybe "near the beginning", I can't remember the phrasing, exactly).  I remember being surprised, thinking maybe more time had passed, so I re-settled in, knowing the trip was soon to start.    And that's when the drums started.  All of a sudden, anxiety surged through my body.  Until this point, I had felt peaceful and calm, if anything, a little restless to begin.  But at this point, the anxiety really kicked in.  I felt a sense of impending doom, like I couldn't escape, and the reminder that I truly could not, the experience was just beginning, and I couldn't leave, even if I wanted to.  The drums felt like a ticking clock, counting down to something bad about to happen.  It felt like when they stopped, time would be up.  ("time" for what, I still don't know)  I took the headphones off because it was too much.  My body was tense, nervous with anticipation.    Suddenly, I was acutely aware, the trip had begun.    I began to really lose sense of time, began to see images that I wasn't sure if were memory, or hallucination.  I can't remember what they were, but I remember verbalizing at this point that I was feeling the sense of impending doom, that I was scared.  They asked if it was a familiar feeling - I said it was.  This is the way I feel most of the time, I replied.  A constant sense of something bad about to happen.  They encouraged me to follow that feeling, and so I did.  It led me back to my childhood gymnastics gym.  I kept getting images of the old coaches office, where the fridge/freezer with the ice packs was.  It was a place I frequented, always injured, always sore.      (Trigger warning for the following content: sexual assault)     I began to think about Ray Adams, a pedophile who coached at my gym for a couple years when I was around 8-10 years old.  I mentioned this, and that I thought it may be a red herring, because I knew that he could not have molested me, I was too young at the time to have been coached by him, and his victims were older than me, not in my group.  I felt a sensation that my body knew something that I couldn't remember, or wished I could forget.  Gisele encouraged me to continue to follow this, I remember her saying, he was around.  And just because it didn't happen to you didn't mean you didn't pick up on the creepy vibes that he likely gave off.  And I talked about how when I was a little older, a few years maybe, the news crews showed up at practice one day, asking us, "Did we remember Ray Adams?".  It's all so blurry, but I remember learning then that he was a pedophile.  I remember at that point becoming suspicious of every male coach, every spot.  I had a few memories flash by of other male coaches, of female coaches not letting us alone with them, and some spots that brushed the side of my breasts, the inside of my groin.  I always brushed them off, they were 1 off incidents and the coaches were not otherwise creepy, but I think the Ray situation put doubt in my mind - it became hard to trust anyone.  I remember thinking that I didn't want to "make up" a situation that wasn't there, making the pieces fit where they did not, so I let myself think back to things I could remember - the thoughts brought me to my injuries.      (TW: Injuries)  I started to remember the backhandspring swing down incident, where I hurt my vagina by splitting the beam.  I saw myself injure myself, felt my body acting out the movements, bringing my hands to face when I mentioned the times I broke my nose by smashing it into the beam (twice), and using my fingers to demonstrate the movements.  About now, I began to shake.  I don't think the shaking stopped until the trip was over.  It was first my legs, writhing around, restless and uneasy.  Eventually, it became my whole body.  Convulsing, as if I were freezing, but I was sweating.  My palms were sweaty, I had chills all over.  I kept thinking back.  I remembered the aftermath of hurting my vagina, how I never saw a doctor, how my peers laughed at me, how embarrassed I felt.  I talked about how I wasn't allowed to cover up at practice, leotards only, but how I got "special permission" because I was falling out of my leotard, so swollen.  I remembered feeling exposed, embarrassed, and trying to be "tough" and not let any of it get to me.  I remembered how scary it felt to know deeply that something was wrong with my body, but that nobody was taking me seriously.  My body was so uncomfortable throughout this time.  I wanted desperately to leave my skin, to not feel the way I was feeling.  It suddenly hit me that this was how my child-self must have felt, way back then, with no way to process those feelings.  They must have felt so scary to her.  I had the thought that my coaches tossed me around like a doll, who could do tricks, with no care for my well-being.  Gisele invited me to use a pillow to protect my tense, private area.  To feel that support, that protection.  To give myself rest that this was in the past, that this was over, it happened, but it was not still happening.  The feeling of doom remained.  I was so sad for my younger self, having to endure such pain.  And that she never got to be a child, she just was an entertainer to my parents, my coaches, the judges.  A tool to be used by my coaches for the sake of winning.  I feel like my body was abused.  I felt grateful for Gisele and Rosanna for holding me throughout this experience, for keeping my child safe.  (As I write this, I feel that sense of doom, that anxiety in my belly, my legs tapping, shaking in my chair).  They encouraged me to look at an image of my child self, to see her, to feel her emotions.  The fear was palpable.  I saw dark, shadowy spirits.  It felt unbearable to be in my skin.  I tried to stay with her, my legs ran in place.  Kicking, fighting.  It felt like I was fighting my pain.     I recalled other injuries as well, particularly breaking my two big toes, despite begging my coach for a spot, and her denying me one.  I remembered how scared I was and how I tried to advocate for myself, and how she mocked me by giving me a "one-finger spot", only to say "I guess you really did need a spot" once I flung off the bar, landed with my toes curled under, unable to stand up again because of the pain.    I recalled breaking my foot in a meet, on the floor exercise, in front of a huge crowd.  I remembered how I didn't stop once I broke my foot even though I couldn't put weight on it, but rather, kept going, and finished the routine, narrowly avoiding breaking my neck on my last tumbling pass.  I had tunnel vision, I didn't notice my coach telling me to stop.  They always told us, if you fall, you get back up, and you finish.  I didn't even consider stopping, or that I was seriously injured.  I was holding back tears the rest of the routine, knowing I wasn't supposed to show the judges if I was in pain.      I recalled how these three injuries impacted me at school, how I was always "the injured one", being carted around in a wheelchair or on crutches or with my feet in shoes or a boot.  How I tried to go to school with my vagina injury, but couldn't stand up for the duration of announcements, the pain was "worse than childbirth", as I remember telling my mom (who reminded me, I couldn't possibly say that, but I still believe it, to this day).  It was as if every time I separated my legs to walk, someone shoved knives up my vagina, into my insides.  I could almost feel that pain, it made my stomach churn and my body tense.     I remember talking through these moments with them, and they were so supportive, reminding me these things were really horrible, and that I needed to release the tension in my body around them.  To let myself shake, to do whatever I needed to do to get it out.  Gisele asked me what sound my child self made when she was scared - I told her I usually stayed quiet, but would inappropriately yell in other circumstances at home.   I noticed my breath catch, get shallow, a slight whimper.  She demonstrated a sound that I followed, allowing a noise to leave my gut that I have never made before, but felt releasing.  I kept going for a while, trying to get out every bit that I could, until I no longer made a sound when I tried.  (I notice a part judging me for doing this, I feel embarrassed at the sound that came out, but I am trying to lean into its beauty instead, for it did release some feelings I'd long forgotten).  I did this and my body continued to shake, and eventually, my jaw began to shake as well, my teeth wanted to grind.  (I asked for my mouthguard, I was scared to do more damage to my TMJ joints and teeth than I already have).  I then let them go to town, and my whole body shook, my teeth grinded.  At some point, I began to yawn.  This might have been later on, I can't remember.    While I recalled these things, everything was so dark.  I can't remember much about what I saw, just that I was so scared.  When I tell these stories in my daily life, I feel as though they could have happened to someone else.  I rarely, if ever, am able to access the way I felt during those awful times.    Eventually, I had to pee, again.  This time, I took my time getting to the bathroom, and this time, the tiles were moving, the walls were breathing, and my eyes looked like saucers.  The visual distortions were all grey, and it felt very unpleasant.     Upon my return, I accidentally saw the time, which said it was 1pm.  I was shocked at how hard I was tripping, thinking, I should be on the come-down by now.  Instead, I was barely at the peak.  Gisele encouraged me to tuck back in, that we shouldn't bring me back too soon.  This was good.  When I returned, while I still felt that panic and doom, things began to shift.  I began to hear birds chirping above me, and to see a bright light open (in my mind's eye, despite the eye shades being on).  I felt the darkness below me, pulling me down, but a voice inside told me to go towards the light.  I told Rosanna, she recalled for me, at this point, I said I felt between two worlds (darkness and peace), and that I wanted to go towards the light, but I was scared to leave little Sam behind.  I didn't want to leave her alone down there.  But I knew I needed to go to the light, that I couldn't bear the darkness anymore.  So I followed the birds.  (I think the birds were in the songs?  I don't think I hallucinated those, but I could be very wrong lol).      The spirits around me guided me towards the light.  There was a sense of iridescent rainbow shimmery strands showing me the way.  Then, the visuals opened up so far that my mind's eye couldn't see anything else.  It was like rivers of square, repeating, gold fractals, covered in gemstones and crystals, took over my visual field.  I couldn't believe what I was seeing, and had the sense immediately that I was witnessing the universe, unfurling before my eyes.  I realized I hadn't lost my sense of self.  That I could tell "I" was the one being "shown" this, like a movie, by the spirit guides of the mushroom.  It almost resembled Buddhist Temples, the ones I saw in Thailand.  (Though when I looked back at pictures after the fact, I couldn't find anything that matched my mind's eye's images.  Some things came close, but it was entirely unique imagery that the mushroom displayed).  Time and space folded in over themselves, flowing like rivers, fractals rushing so fast across my visual field that I couldn't keep up with any of them, individually.  There was a sensation of 'church' and 'sacrament', the realization that this was like what the "eucharist" is supposed to reveal, but never could, because it isn't connected to the worlds beyond like the mushroom is.  I remember thinking, this is what organized religions are missing.  The core of it all, the truth of the universe.  I remember a feeling of awe and wonder washing over me.  I realized this is behind what I see in my daily life, beyond the projection of reality, it's made up of beautiful fractals, folding in on themselves, flowing like rivers.  I was amazed.    Things opened up into what resembled an "airport", with terminals as far as the mind could see.  Only instead of seeing "airport" things, I just saw archways and expanding grid-like webs along the ground.  It was purple and blue.  But with the sense of brightness, not darkness.  I saw visions of deities and elephants, with long trunks, adorned in jewels.  The images were fast and fleeting, I am sure I'm not remembering all of them.  It was like they were flowing through a never ending tunnel, with lightness in the middle and above.  There was a feeling of a maternal presence, guiding me.  It felt like a movie that I couldn't stop watching, even if I wanted to, but by this point, I didn't want to.  I could've watched for as long as it would have shown me.  I felt a lightness in my body, almost as if I was floating above myself on the couch.    It felt hard to come back to my physical body, the anxieties returning once the lightness went away.  It felt disconcerting coming back to the hospital basement, I felt nervous.  I was seeing geometric patterns along the walls, and the shadowy figures came back.  None of these were clear, it was almost as if I was sensing them, more than "seeing" them.  But I could "see" them, briefly, nonetheless.  I was looking around the room, while Gisele and Rosanna were coaxing me back to a grounded place, a centered place, in the basement.  I struggled to ground because of the visual distortions.  I went back to the bathroom, noticing the tiles still shadowy, and still breathing.  I was scared, again.  This time, because I didn't know why I was STILL tripping.  I remember asking them to retake my blood pressure to reassure me I was okay.    The knit blanket I was under was moving, the knit pattern flowing like a river along the pattern.  I recall, in the depths of the trip, when I would pull the blanket over my side, it felt like the blankets place in space dictated the visual fields edges.  At this point, I was chatting with Gisele and Rosanna, telling them how I was ready to go home, but how I felt weird, concerningly so.  I said it felt like coming out of anesthesia, wonky, out of body, out of place.  It wasn't the light, twinkly, pleasant afterglow that I was used to.  It was scary, and that scared me.    I asked to turn the music off, and they turned it down.  It felt like it was keeping me in the trip, and all I wanted was to facilitate the comedown.  I remember feeling eager to stop tripping and to get to a comfortable and familiar place, wanting to see my partner.  Feeling like I would feel okay again once I was out of there, and with her, knowing the drugs would wear off, and that my anxiety was just high because I was in limbo, remembering I was a research participant, knowing the business day was over, knowing we needed to get home.  I tried to let those fears fall away, it was difficult to do so.    Throughout the experience, I felt I could not tell if my eyes were open or closed, at many points.  And at a point in which I was seeing the golden riches of the universe's fabric, I noticed my eyes were wet with tears.  I wiped them away, but they kept coming.  I didn't "feel like" I was crying, but the tears were definitely there.  Also at some point, I was guided to bring my feet to the edge of the couch, to feel its support, to use it to put pressure on the soles of my feet, to kick and stomp and run (while laying down, safely).  They put pillows under my knees. I remember they asked how my body felt, including my back, and I said it was tense.  I kicked until it dissipated.  I was scared to keep going deeper, finding the fear of how much trauma is stored within me, how deep the well goes.  The whole time, it felt as though I could not stop the thoughts from coming, nor control the direction they went.  I was succumbing to the experience, despite being scared to do so.    At some point towards the end, they brought the doctor in to talk to me and reassure me that I was okay.  That the psilocybin was just metabolizing slower than it does for others.  I still don't understand how it lasted 8+ hours - I've never had a mushroom trip last more than 6.  They brought me some amazing chia pudding, it felt like my blood sugar was dropping rapidly, and I was feeling malnourished.  The chia pudding was so good, the mint and grapefruit smelled amazing, and it tasted so good.  It was easy to eat and I was grateful there was no added sugars.  I ate as much as I could stomach, which was a little more than 1.  I wasn't nauseous, but it was hard to eat.  They also made me tea, which warmed my soul.  I remember yawning a LOT as I came out of it.  My palms weren't sweaty anymore.    The survey was next, which took me a few tries to get through.  The iPad made me feel motion sick.  I could see the words and I could read them, but it took a lot of mental effort to understand what I was reading, despite the questions being very basic.  It was jarring to be reminded of technology so soon after a trip.  It was hard to answer the questions without them bringing up visceral feelings from the trip, which kept prompting me to need a break.    During the trip, my energy was low, I felt stuck to the couch, only able to get up when I felt the need to pee, and only then after waiting some time until I really had to get up.  I shook most of the day, I alternated between feeling really cold and sweating.  I remember towards the end, someone (the music?) singing, "I love you" over and over again, I couldn't tell if it was the music, or if I had imagined it.  It sounded like multiple voices.  There were birds chirping; it was so peaceful.  I felt held.    I tried to tell the little girl, it was okay to move on with our life, that we deserved it.    On Friday, I woke up with no pain, and my pains have not returned as of writing this email.  I don't anticipate this will last forever, but I have been really comfortable, feeling my body to be lighter than it was before.  I am skeptical about its absence.  I did experience some abdominal/pelvic pain, like a dull ache, cramping sensation, from Friday night-Saturday night.  I am not sure if it was uterine pain or gas pain, but it has since resolved on Sunday.  I am doubtful it was related and rather coincidental, but who knows.  I have had a few spurts of anxiety, though I have had more success than normal in quieting those voices.  I talked to the narrator/rehasher part on Friday (before integration) who wanted to go over every detail of the trip over and over, let them know it was okay to relax, that there would be time to think and rehash, and that constantly ruminating was not helping, but I understood they wanted to keep me safe, somehow, by doing that.  I thanked the part for trying to help, but asked it to give me some space.  I did this 3-4 times before I finally found some peace and quiet.  Normally, talking to the parts doesn't really give them the freedom to relax, but it felt like I had more control over my mind, for once.  I have had some bodily sensation anxiety, like a growling in the stomach and gut and chest, that naws and probes and prods.    Some insights I've gained.  It feels as though I've "white knuckled" my way through life.  It has been so stressful, and so hard on me.  I was, as Gisele wisely put it, "a fish in water".  I worry that I may still be, and that all the choices I've made since adulthood are just the illusion of choice.  This thought is painful, I hope that I do not spend the next 20 years healing from the last 10, the way I am currently healing from the first 20.  During the trip, I tried to let go of "being mentally tough" and let my body somatically express what it needed to.  I've noticed a judging part since the trip, who is embarrassed by the way I acted, the way I couldn't hold it together.  Rosanna said that I approached the trip courageously - I am trying to internalize that, instead.    I don't have to be good to be worthy of life.  Life isn't about pleasing anyone or being good at anything.  I can be active and athletic without being Olympic level, or perfect.  I can do things with bad form, and it won't kill me.  As long as I try my best to move intentionally, with purpose, I have already won.  The airport imagery reminded me that I can always make different choices.  I never have to be stuck in one place, I can choose another path as soon as I realize the one I am on is no longer serving me.  I realized the sense of impending doom has been with me since a young age, when I was a little girl, receiving one set of verbal messages, but another set of sensed feelings.  This has left me in a state of confusion that is triggered all the time in my adulthood.  I feel like I never understand what's happening to me or around me.  I think, and hope, this journey will allow that trigger to ease up.  To be a reminder, it's just choices.  It's not life or death.  The world is not out to get me.  I am at the exact right place, at the exact right time.     I am proud of myself for having gone through so much and for still wanting to try to be better, and to know myself deeper.  Despite the pain that it causes to go there.  I hope this has unlocked some access to these feelings I have long been unable to reach.  I thought my physical body could not bear to access these pains, but it did, and it held me through it.  It is in the past now.  I'm noticing a distance between "me" and "my thoughts" that I have always wanted to find.  It's barely perceptible, but it is there.  My "intellectualizer" is present, trying to think through the events.  I am trying to set her aside so that I can feel.  I've also sensed a judger, wondering if my experience was "more intense" than "it should have been", since I came back.  Wondering how it compared to other participants' journeys.  I am reminding those parts, it is my journey, and it is the right intensity, at the right time.    I am sure more happened than I can recall, but I think this is the best I can do.  Pardon the length, I basically copied my journal entries from the last few days, and then some.  If I missed any types of things you need, let me know, I can do my best to elaborate.

tsqp_6: I believe that during the session I was able to process, at the somatic level, pains and injuries from my childhood that were traumatic in nature, that I had previously been unable to release.  In hindsight, it became apparent that when I was reacting to my current pains, I was clouded by memories of past pains, that worsened the cycle of present-pain.  Though the trip was ultimately exhausting and challenging, I felt lighter after finishing it, and I do not feel stuck on my childhood injuries.  I am seemingly able to associate them better as "past" events, rather than events that may still be causing me pain, today.
tsqp_7: The lack of ability to alter the trip to my personal needs due to the nature of reproducible research, especailly pertaining to setting.  Not having windows or sunshine felt like it made the trip 'darker', and not being able to change the song when it was terrifying, but having to fully subject myself to that, was really hard.  Ultimately, in hindsight, I'm so proud I was able to get through this experience despite the fear, and I feel more equipped to manage such feelings of doom and fear, as I was able to move through them despite it being hard.
tsqp_8: I feel more hope for the future.
tsqp_9: I did not like the REDCap survey at the end of the trip - sliding the bar made me feel motion sick, and i had to stop to rest like 3-4x in the middle of the survey.  At this point, I was getting exceedingly anxious to leave, as I was there longer than I expected, and I was anxious to get back to my partner and a familiar environment.  I felt like the REDCap quetsions kept "reviving" my trip,  and I was still having a hard time using electronics (bc of visual effects), and all I wanted was to be done for the day, after such an exhausting experience.  Also, the processed snacks offered at the end of the day  were not appropriate nutritionally to support the comedown after not eating all day (luckily, my facilitators had chia pudding, so I was able to eat that, and was quite grateful for it).
tsqp_10: It did make me more anxious than I had expected on the day of going into the trip knowing that I didn't know what combination of substances I would receive.  Additionally, it was weird not knowing how much psilocybin I was about to consume.  The facilitators were amazing though, nothing but positive things to say about them both!

dosejournal_reflectiontext_edcdaf: Describe your experience during the dosing session from beginning to end with as much detail as possible.    I began to feel sleepy pretty soon after dosing and laid down within 15 minutes of dosing. I probably started using the eye mask ten or so minutes later. I can't remember much from the dosing session but mostly experienced light visualizations that changed frequently with changes in the music (felt like every fifteen seconds or so). These were rarely personal - mostly random shapes and colors, almost like an old Windows screensaver. Body felt very relaxed and cozy with minimal back pain during the experience. There were two thoughts that stood out during dosing, otherwise I mostly remember having my blood pressure checked, using the restroom, and asking a question about the music. I felt dizzy and a little unstable the first time I went to use the restroom but mostly fine. I felt pretty lucid walking and seeing myself in the mirror, nothing crazy. The two personal/introspective moments I remember during the dosing related to thoughts that I should be more accommodating of my need for high stimulation / frequent boredom. I tried to direct my thoughts toward my family history or chronic pain but it wouldn't stick and my attention would return to the visualizations. I may have had auditory hallucinations but it was hard to tell given the music. I did feel quite aware of the music the entire time, I didn't feel that my attention shifted away to the extent that I wasn't listening to any given song. Near the end of the dosing session once I felt quite normal I did a little stretching on my yoga mat. I debriefed with the two facilitators for maybe 20-30 minutes at the end of the session before checking out.     Describe your emotions, energy levels, and thoughts during and after the dosing session.   I described these briefly above but again, felt pretty sleepy and out of it during the dosing session but don't think I fell asleep at any point. Emotions were mellow, impersonal/detached. Very few verbal thoughts, mostly visualizations. After the dosing session I felt pretty emotionless/numb until later at night (around 9 pm). I took a long nap after I got home and had a late lunch, then slept a lot again overnight. I felt disappointed with my dosing experience which I discussed with the facilitators after the sessions.     Describe if you encountered any challenging emotions, insights, or sensations throughout the session.   No memorable emotions or insights arose during the session, which felt very strange. Sensations were pleasant and comfortable but I mostly felt like I was in the falling asleep state of mind the entire time.    Summarize any changes in health that may have occurred since the dosing session.   No observable changes in health since the dosing session. I had a big headache most of the following day and have felt tired, but otherwise nothing significant.

dosejournal_reflectiontext_edcdaf: I entered the building with a slightly elevated feeling of anxiety. I think this was due to the fact I  had highly caffeinated Nespresso drinks. This was coupled with a bit of worry since I did not  know what to expect. My only reference to psilocybin was pop culture shows, and the reading  that I had done about medical applications and therapies. I was also a little anxious after the  pharmacy had called me with the list of rescue medications that had been prescribed to me.  I felt really comfortable with Ashley and Andrew. It was easy to explain my elevated feeling of  anxiety to them. The room was comfortable, and my personal pillows worked perfectly. One  pillow is a wedge shape for lying in an incline, and the other pillow was like a pentagonal prism,  for supporting my knees. I use these supports to help minimize my back pain when resting.  The grounding session was relaxing and helped me with my anxiety a bit.  When I took the pills, I took them one at a time and drank a lot of water. It almost felt like some  were sticking in my throat, so I needed a refill of my water bottle and drank some more.  When I laid back into the blankets and pillows, I felt a little nervous again. I put on the black out  mask and the headphones, I asked for the volume to be turned down a lot, I have always been  sensitive to the volume of headphones. I noticed that the blackout mask was not completely  blacking out light, it may have been because I do not like masks to be tight on my face. I  focused on my breath to ground myself through the anxiety I felt. After a few minutes, I  remember a distinct shift from the anxiety end of the excitement spectrum to more of a hopeful  and positive feeling anticipation. During this shift, I felt an all over calm and relaxed feeling. The  first thing I saw was purple amorphous lights in a black or dark space. They seemed to be  traveling away from me as the started out large and shrinking into the distance, this happened  in a pattern, one after another, with the next one appearing large as the last one disappeared.  This is similar to something I experience sometimes at night when my eyes are adjusting to the  dark at bedtime, however normally there is no color to this, it is more dark and less dark waves.  In the session, I remembered a point when the purple stopped going away from me, and  instead started a rhythmic progression toward me, until my whole visual field was purple. I  remember needing to use the restroom after what seemed like a long time, but it had not been  as I had not yet had my blood pressure checked. I could only clearly see images when my eyes  were closed and the blindfold was on. They were very faint when I opened my eyes with the  blindfold on. Each time I took off the blindfold, there were no visual or audible differences at all.  The only thing I noticed when I did get up to go to the bathroom was a slight floaty feeling, I  was surprised that there was nothing else noticeable with the headphones and blindfold off.  I remembered having to use the bathroom a lot. Since I did not see anything out of the ordinary  while the blindfold and headphones were off, I almost expected to not see anything again when  I put them back on.  At the end of the purple experience, I did start to notice some blue spots that seemed to  morph into triangular shapes. I remember many layers to things, but I do not recall the order.  The overall space was black, and the images I experienced were all in a black space. I  remember seeing 2 light blue layers, almost as if I was standing in a crack in an ice sheet,  looking up at the black sky, with ice on left and right. I remember seeing layers in neutral colors  much like what you would see if you were looking at an unclose image of Jupiter, each layer  had tiny details in it, and the layers and details were moving in different directions. I remember  seeing a distinct base of a giant redwood tree. I also remember seeing a corner of a building  with pillars, it seemed to have been covered in mussels.  I felt a lot of wonder, curiosity, and calm. A recurrent theme was the presence of someone, not  really a person with defined characteristics, I just knew of the presence. It seemed like they  were wanting me to see them, but not get to close. Eventually, I realized that this person was  me, or a version of me that existed before the trauma of the world set into my life. The version  of me that I stopped showing up for many years ago.  I was a little disappointed that the experience did not go further than this. But, I was happy that  I did not have a bad experience, I had been worried about possibly having a feeling like being  trapped in a night terror, as I have those on occasion.  I think my experience highlighted that I am always showing up for so many people, but I often  do this at the cost of putting myself and my goals on the back-burner. It is hard to be the one  who always does so much for others, but they do not show up for me, I guess it highlighted  that I am tired of this and the attendant disappointment.  I remember the room seeming really cold. I was bundled up in all the blankets. I was wearing  sweats and socks, too. I think that the cold may have influenced my glacier or ice sheet  experience. I had a slight headache during the end of the experience. At times, I had a little  pain in my right heel. Other than that, it was a pleasant experience in regard to physical  sensations.  Overall, I really enjoyed the experience.  I had some headaches and slight nausea after the session on Tuesday and needed to take  extra strength acetaminophen. On Wednesday, I had slight headaches during the day and a  little nausea at bedtime. I was pretty exhausted on Wednesday, and I took it easy and rested. I  seemed to also experience a little more sensitivity to light for a couple days after the session. I  have been really thirsty since the session, but that is okay as I have been trying to make a  conscious effort to drink more water. I have not been hesitating to tell people what is on my  mind, like I normally do. I feel like I have been sleeping pretty well. I bet I might have a little  Sunday night anxiety when I go to bed tonight (many teachers talk about experiencing this), as  I go back to work after having a week off for Thanksgiving Break.
